name: Starts 0, 4 and contains no 3-term arithmetic progression.
comment: This is what would now be called the Stanley Sequence S(0,4). See A185256.
reference: R. K. Guy, Unsolved Problems in Number Theory, E10.
N. J. A. Sloane and Simon Plouffe, The Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences, Academic Press, 1995 (includes this sequence).

mathematica: ss[s1_, M_] := Module[{n, chvec, swi, p, s2, i, j, t1, mmm}, t1 = Length[s1]; mmm = 1000; s2 = Table[s1, {t1 + M}] // Flatten; chvec = Array[0&, mmm]; For[i = 1 , i <= t1 , i++, chvec[[s2[[i]] ]] = 1]; (* get n-th term *) For[n = t1+1 , n <= t1 + M , n++, (* try i as next term *) For[i = s2[[n-1]] + 1 , i <= mmm , i++, swi = -1; (* test against j-th term *) For[ j = 1 , j <= n-2 , j++, p = s2[[n - j]]; If[ 2*p - i < 0 , Break[] ]; If[ chvec[[2*p - i]] == 1 , swi = 1; Break[] ] ]; If[ swi == -1 , s2[[n]] = i; chvec[[i]] = 1; Break[] ] ]; If[ swi == 1 , Print["Error, no solution at n = ", n] ] ]; Table[s2[[i]], {i, 1, t1+M}] ]; ss[{0, 4}, 80] (* _Jean-François Alcover_, Sep 10 2013, translated from Maple program given in A185256 *)
author: _N. J. A. Sloane_
